title: Methodology
text: one study arm mean change μ\mu, standard deviation σ\sigma minimal important difference (MID) threshold mm, assume patient-level change XX Normally distributed. responder patient whose change crosses threshold. responder probability p=Pr⁡(X>m)=Φ(μ−mσ)(higher change better), p = \Pr(X > m) = \Phi\!\left(\frac{\mu - m}{\sigma}\right) \quad\text{(higher change better),} p=Φ(m−μσ)p = \Phi\!\left(\frac{m - \mu}{\sigma}\right) lower change better. cut-point (“dichotomization”) method reviewed Thorlund colleagues (2011) detailed Anzures-Cabrera, Sarpatwari & Higgins (2011). -arm contrast familiar binary effect measure: default risk difference RD=pe−pc\mathrm{RD} = p_e - p_c. respondeR keeps proportions [0,1][0, 1] scale internally converts percentages display.

"delta": propagates uncertainty estimated mean SD Normal CDF, Var̂(p)=ϕ()2[1n+a22(n−1)]\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(p) = \phi()^2\left[\frac{1}{n} + \frac{^2}{2(n-1)}\right] =(μ−m)/σa = (\mu - m)/\sigma. "delta" form , generally preferable summary-statistic inputs; "binomial" default continuity earlier results. defensible method respects study’s scale.

title: Methodology
text: Pool dichotomizing. mean combined inverse variance SD within-study pooled SD: d‾⋆=∑id‾/vi∑i1/vi,vi=si2ni;s⋆=∑(ni−1)si2∑(ni−1). \bar d^{\star} = \frac{\sum_i \bar d_i / v_i}{\sum_i 1/v_i},\; v_i = \frac{s_i^2}{n_i}; \qquad s^{\star} = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_i (n_i - 1)\, s_i^2}{\sum_i (n_i - 1)}}. p⋆=Φ((d‾⋆−m)/s⋆)p^{\star} = \Phi((\bar d^{\star} - m)/s^{\star}) risk-difference variance comes delta method, propagating uncertainty pooled mean pooled SD, Var(p⋆)≈(∂p⋆∂μ)2Var(d‾⋆)+(∂p⋆∂σ)2Var(s⋆),Var(s⋆)≈s⋆22∑(ni−1). \mathrm{Var}(p^{\star}) \approx \left(\frac{\partial p^{\star}}{\partial \mu}\right)^2 \mathrm{Var}(\bar d^{\star}) + \left(\frac{\partial p^{\star}}{\partial \sigma}\right)^2 \mathrm{Var}(s^{\star}), \qquad \mathrm{Var}(s^{\star}) \approx \frac{s^{\star 2}}{2 \sum_i (n_i - 1)} .  Including SD term keeps method consistent individual delta method avoids intervals narrow. paper-aligned “pool--dichotomize” estimator.

title: Methodology
text: Choosing MID can contentious. common-language effect size (CLES, probabilistic index) probability randomly chosen treated patient better change randomly chosen control. Normal model exact: CLES=Φ(δ),δ=μe−μcσe2+σc2. \mathrm{CLES} = \Phi(\delta), \qquad \delta = \frac{\mu_e - \mu_c}{\sqrt{\sigma_e^2 + \sigma_c^2}}. Per-study δi\delta_i pooled inverse variance (delta-method variance) back-transformed. threshold required.

title: Methodology
text: individual SMD methods pool across studies can use random effects (pooling = "random"). respondeR offers DerSimonian-Laird (closed-form, dependency-free) REML (tau_method = "REML", via metafor), reports Cochran’s QQ, I2I^2, τ2\tau^2 prediction interval. Prediction intervals use tk−2t_{k-2} critical value unstable studies; interpret cautiously kk small. pooled confidence interval , default Normal (Wald) interval can -cover kk small, τ2\tau^2 poorly estimated. Set ci_method = "hksj" Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval, tt-based interval whose width adapts observed dispersion study estimates better calibrated -study meta-analyses (Rover, Knapp & Friede, 2015). example three studies, exactly matters.

MID far observed means can make responder probability equal exactly 0 1, make log ratios, logits inverse-variance weights non-finite. respondeR reports proportions risk difference unclamped, clamps probabilities feed ratios, logs variances away 0 1 tiny amount, sensitivity sweep MID returns finite (wide) results instead failing.

what: Per-study results and a forest plot
title: Getting started with respondeR
text: responder_rd_individual() returns per-study risk differences feed forest plot:
code: responder_rd_individual(sample_responder_data, mid = 1) #>     study       p_e       p_c        rd         se      ci_lb     ci_ub #> 1 Study 1 0.4867232 0.2564577 0.2302655 0.10023645 0.03380566 0.4267253 #> 2 Study 2 0.4355507 0.2259278 0.2096229 0.05454152 0.10272350 0.3165223 #> 3 Study 3 0.5068639 0.2047187 0.3021452 0.05106129 0.20206690 0.4022235 ps <- responder_rd_individual(sample_responder_data, mid = 1) pooled <- responder_analysis(sample_responder_data, mid = 1, method = "individual")  y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(ps) + 1)) est <- c(ps$rd, pooled$rd) * 100 lo  <- c(ps$ci_lb, pooled$rd_lb) * 100 hi  <- c(ps$ci_ub, pooled$rd_ub) * 100 labels <- c(as.character(ps$study), "Pooled")  op <- par(mar = c(4, 6, 1, 1)) plot(NA, xlim = range(c(lo, hi, 0)), ylim = c(0.5, length(y) + 0.5),      yaxt = "n", xlab = "Risk difference (%)", ylab = "", bty = "n") abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey60") segments(lo, y, hi, y, lwd = 2) points(est, y, pch = c(rep(15, nrow(ps)), 18), cex = c(rep(1.4, nrow(ps)), 2)) axis(2, at = y, labels = labels, las = 1, tick = FALSE) par(op)

what: A real example: VAS pain after exercise therapy
title: Getting started with respondeR
text: package bundles real dataset, vas_pain: 20 randomized trials exercise spinal health pooled visual analogue scale (VAS) pain outcome Li, Bao, Wang Zhao (2025). change scores post minus baseline VAS 0 10 cm scale, negative value larger pain reduction; analyze direction = "lower" negative MID equal responder threshold. Using 1.5 cm reduction minimal important difference: , pooling per-study estimates, roughly 17 21 exercise patients per 100 reach 1.5 cm pain reduction controls, depending method. threshold-free common-language effect size avoids picking cut-point: (Data Li et al. (2025), Frontiers Sports Active Living, , Figure 3, reproduced CC 4.0.)
code: res <- responder_analysis(vas_pain, mid = -1.5, direction = "lower",                           pooling = "random", ci_method = "hksj") format_responder_results(res) #>            Method   PE   PC                  RD                  RR #> 1      Individual    -    - 17.5 (10.6 to 24.3) 1.19 (1.08 to 1.32) #> 2   Weighted mean 84.4 63.4 21.0 (18.2 to 23.7) 1.33 (1.28 to 1.38) #> 3 Unweighted mean 78.7 47.1                31.6                1.67 #> 4          Median 83.9 37.3                46.7                2.25 #>                    OR #> 1 3.22 (2.27 to 4.57) #> 2 3.11 (2.63 to 3.68) #> 3                4.14 #> 4                8.81 cles <- responder_cles(vas_pain, direction = "lower") sprintf("A treated patient has less pain than a control %.0f%% of the time (%.0f%% to %.0f%%)",         100 * cles$cles, 100 * cles$cles_lb, 100 * cles$cles_ub) #> [1] "A treated patient has less pain than a control 71% of the time (68% to 74%)"

title: Responder Analysis for Continuous Outcomes
text: respondeR re-expresses meta-analyses continuous trial outcomes terms responders. Clinicians patients reason “many people get better”, standardized mean differences. uses summary statistics trials usually report: mean change, standard deviation sample size arm. respondeR estimates proportion patients whose change crosses minimal important difference (MID) threshold, contrasts arms risk difference (RD), risk ratio (RR), odds ratio () number needed treat (NNT). follows interpretability tutorial Thorlund, Walter, Johnston, Furukawa & Guyatt (2011), implementing cut-point (“dichotomization”) standardized-mean-difference conversions reviews, adds threshold-free common-language effect size. estimation methods evaluated simulation study (Sofi-Mahmudi, 2024). Try browser (install): https://choxos.github.io/respondeR/app/ Documentation: https://choxos.github.io/respondeR/

title: respondeR: Responder Analysis for Continuous Outcomes — respondeR-package
text: package converts continuous trial outcomes (mean change, standard deviation sample size per arm, across studies) proportion "responders": patients whose change crosses minimal important difference (MID) threshold, Normal model change scores. expresses -arm contrast risk difference (RD). Four pooling strategies provided (median, unweighted mean, weighted mean individual), following interpretability methods reviewed Thorlund colleagues (2011) cut-point ("dichotomization") standardized-mean-difference approaches Anzures-Cabrera, Sarpatwari Higgins (2011). statistical engine lives exported, side-effect-free functions (responder_analysis(), responder_proportions(), responder_rd_individual(), responder_cles()) results reproducible unit tested independently bundled Shiny application (launch_responder_analysis()).

title: Responder analysis of continuous trial outcomes — responder_analysis
text: Converts continuous outcomes (mean change, SD sample size per arm, across studies) responder proportions range -arm effect measures: risk difference (RD), risk ratio (RR), odds ratio () number needed treat (NNT), parametric model change scores. Responders defined minimal important difference (MID) threshold (cut-point / "dichotomization" approach Anzures-Cabrera, Sarpatwari Higgins, 2011). threshold-free alternative see responder_cles().

Defaults first four. se_method Per-study SE model "individual": "binomial" (default) "delta". "binomial" variance p(1 - p) / n pseudo-binomial approximation: p probability implied estimated mean SD, proportion observed dichotomized patients, include uncertainty reported mean SD. "delta" propagates uncertainty generally preferable summary-statistic inputs; "binomial" default continuity earlier results. pooling "fixed" (default) "random" effects, "individual" "smd" methods. tau_method -study variance estimator pooling = "random": "DL" (DerSimonian-Laird, default) "REML" (needs metafor package; falls back DL warning unavailable). dist Change-score distribution: "normal" (default), "lognormal" "t". df Degrees freedom dist = "t". mid_sd Optional standard deviation MID threshold; > 0 uncertainty propagated effect-measure variances. ci_type "wald" (default) "logit" (keeps proportion risk-difference intervals within valid bounds via logit transform Newcombe's MOVER method). ci_method Random-effects interval method: "wald" (Normal, default) "hksj" (Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman, t-based interval better calibrated number studies small). conf_level Confidence level (default 0.95).

title: Responder analysis of continuous trial outcomes — responder_analysis
text: individual Dichotomize study, pool per-study effect measures (fixed random effects). defensible option; per-study SE follows se_method. weighted Pool mean change inverse variance SD within-study pooled SD, dichotomize pooled summaries, obtain variances delta method. unweighted, median Dichotomize arithmetic mean / median study means SDs. Summaries variance model: intervals NA. smd Pool standardized mean difference (Hedges' g), bridge odds ratio via logistic link (lnOR = (pi / sqrt(3)) g), combine weighted-pooled control responder rate recover risks. second approach reference; included default. control proportion always uses pooling experimental arm.

title: Common-language effect size (probabilistic index) — responder_cles
text: threshold-free responder-type measure: probability randomly chosen treated patient better change score randomly chosen control. Normal model exact, \(\mathrm{CLES} = \Phi(\delta)\) \(\delta = (\mu_e - \mu_c) / \sqrt{\sigma_e^2 + \sigma_c^2}\) (sign flipped direction = "lower"). Per-study \(\delta\) values pooled fixed- random-effect inverse variance back-transformed, minimal important difference required.

title: respondeR 0.1.0
text: First public release. package began life small Shiny app; release rebuilds documented, tested R package statistics pure, exported functions Shiny app thin front end.

title: respondeR 0.1.0
text: response external methodology audit: Boundary handling. Extreme MIDs push responder probability exactly 0 1 longer crash return infinite intervals; probabilities clamped away 0 1 feed logs, logits weights, reported proportions risk difference stay unclamped. Small-study random effects. Added ci_method = "hksj" Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval, better calibrated Wald number studies small. Weighted-method variance now propagates uncertainty pooled SD well pooled mean (full delta method), intervals longer narrow. Weighted confidence intervals slightly wider first build; point estimates unchanged. Stricter validation. Sample sizes must whole numbers; lognormal model now rejects negative study-arm mean changes aggregation; vector building blocks reject non-finite sd/n. binomial SE documented pseudo-binomial approximation, delta recommended summary-statistic inputs.

title: respondeR 0.1.0
text: responder_analysis(): main entry point. Converts continuous arm summaries (mean change, SD, n) responder proportions tidy table -arm effect measures: risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio number needed treat. Pooling methods: "individual", "weighted", "unweighted", "median" "smd". responder_rd_individual() responder_proportions(): exported building blocks per-study risk differences arm responder probabilities. responder_cles(): threshold-free common-language effect size (probabilistic index), pooled fixed random effects, requiring MID. format_responder_results(): display-ready formatting reports app. launch_responder_analysis(): launches bundled ResponderAnalysis Shiny application (direction toggle, method/pooling/interval options, RR//NNT, per-study forest plot, CLES CSV /O). sample_responder_data: small bundled example dataset. vas_pain: real bundled dataset 20 exercise--spinal-health trials pooled VAS pain scale (Li et al., 2025, doi:10.3389/fspor.2025.1614906, reproduced CC 4.0).

title: respondeR 0.1.0
text: Random effects. individual SMD methods support fixed- random-effects pooling (pooling = "random") DerSimonian-Laird (dependency-free) REML (tau_method = "REML", via metafor) -study variance, reporting Cochran’s Q, -squared, tau-squared prediction interval. Relative measures. Risk ratio odds ratio (log-scale pooling) number needed treat (Altman, 1998) accompany absolute risk difference. SMD bridge. "smd" method pools standardized mean difference (Hedges’ g) maps odds ratio logistic link, combined weighted-pooled control risk (Cox; Chinn, 2000). Refinements. Logit-transformed proportion intervals Newcombe MOVER risk-difference intervals (ci_type = "logit"); propagation uncertainty MID threshold (mid_sd); alternative change-score distributions (dist = "lognormal" "t").

what: Statistical corrections (results differ from the previous app)
title: respondeR 0.1.0
text: earlier Shiny app contained several errors fixed . Numbers weighted unweighted methods, confidence intervals, differ app; individual median point estimates unchanged. control responder proportion now computed pooling experimental arm (previously every method reused median method’s control proportion). weighted method now pools SD within-study pooled SD sqrt(sum((n-1) sd^2) / sum(n-1)) rather inverse-variance pooling SDs, delta-method variance risk difference. median unweighted methods reported point-estimate summaries (variance model) instead carrying spurious interval. Proportions kept [0, 1] scale internally, removing class percent-scale variance errors.
